Rise in pollution in river Yamuna
†*316. CH. SUKHRAM SINGH
Y ADA V: Will the Minister of W A TER
RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT
AND GANGA REJUVENATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that water of
Yamuna river is getting polluted, day-by-
day, despite various cleaning schemes and
due to rise in pollution and muck in the
river, the ground water level and its quality
has deteriorated in Delhi;
(b) whether the Ammonia level in the
water of Yamuna river has risen to such
an extent that it is not even potable for
animals; and
(c) the details of  expenditure during
the last three years on maintaining
clealiness and purity of Yamuna and
results thereof?
Monitoring mechanism for
implementation of schemes
†*317. SHRIMATI SAMPATIYA
UIKEY: Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
is considering to establish a special
monitoring mechanism for better
implementation of schemes at Panchayat
level;
(b) if so, the steps being taken by
Government in this direction;
(c) whether Government is also
considering to provide technical training
to employees posted in rural areas; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

AIBP funds for Tamil Nadu
*318. SHRIMATI SASIKALA
PUSHPA: Will the Minister of  WATER
RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT
AND GANGA REJUVENATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has allocated
any funds to Tamil Nadu Government
under Accelerated Irrigation Benefit
Programme (AIBP) to construct a new
flood carrier canal from the existing
Kannadian Canal located in Vellankuzhi in
Ambasamudram T aluk of Tirunelveli
District;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Drying up of water streams from
Himalayas
†*319. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will
the Minister of WA TER RESOURCES,
RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA
REJUVENATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of
NITI Aayog’s report which states that 60
per cent of water streams, including the
Ganges and the Brahamputra, coming from
Himalayas, are on the verge of drying up;
(b) whether drying up of streams is
due to retreat of glaciers on account of
climate change, increasing demand of
water, changes in land due to deforestation
and changes in tectonic plates;
(c) whether five crore people in twelve
States, dependent on these streams would
be facing drinking water crisis in the next
ten years; and
(d) if so, steps being taken by
Government in this regard?
Construction of roads and bridges in
Assam by NHIDCL
*320. SHRI BHUBANESWAR
KALITA: Will the Minister of ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the National
Highways and Infrastructure
Development Corporation Ltd.
(NHIDCL) has been entrusted with the
work of construction of roads and bridges
in Assam;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the financial allocation for each work;
(c) whether it is also a fact that all the
works are running far behind schedule
resulting in time and cost overrun; and
(d) if so, the action proposed by
Government to accelerate the work
progress?
Environment clearance for irrigation
projects in Maharashtra
*321. SHRI SAMBHAJI
CHHATRAPATI : W ill the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND
CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state:
(a) whether a number of proposals
pertaining to irrigation in Maharashtra are
pending with Government since 2011;
(b) if so, the details thereof with reasons
for not according clearance so far despite
the fact that better irrigation facilities
would have drastically improved the
economic condition of farmers;

Decline in defence expenditure
3361. SHRI VEER SINGH: Will the
Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that defence
expenditure as a percentage of Gross
Domestic Product (GDP) has been
declining over the past few years;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government is considering
to increase the defence expenditure; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Attacks on army camps
3362. SHRI DEREK O’BRIEN: Will
the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of attacks on army
camps that have occurred during the last
three years and number of soldiers who
have died in the attacks;
(b) the reasons for these attacks;
(c) whether it is a fact that army combat
uniforms are easily available in the market,
if so, steps Government is taking to monitor
their sale;
(d) the measures Government is taking
to ensure garrison security;
(e) whether Government has
implemented the recommendations of the
Lt. Gen. Philip Campose committee's
Report, 2016, if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor?
Defence manufacturing under 'Make
in India'
3363. SHRI HARIVANSH: Will the
Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has received
any proposals from any State Government
for promoting defence manufacturing
under 'Make in India' programme; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

789
Approval for manufacture of small
arms
3364. DR. V . MAITREYAN: Will the
Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has
received any letters from Members of
Parliament as regards delay in according
approval to the MoU proposal  with
Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM)
for the manufacture of small arms Non-
Prohibited Bore (NPB) pistols;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
response of Government thereto;
(c) whether any probe with regards to
the company verification by Government
in the facility of the OEM on 2 August,
2017 had been conducted; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
status of the probe?
Return of MoU by Government
3365. DR. V . MAITREYAN: Will the
Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ordnance Factory
Board (OFB) had given any specific
explanation to Government in its reply
dated 24 October, 2017 with regards to the
returning of a MoU proposal by
Government in its letter dated 25.07.2017;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
response of Government to that reply;
(c) whether the Department of Defence
Production had discussed this issue further
in its subsequent board meetings; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
SoP followed in OFBs
3366. DR. V . MAITREYAN: Will the
Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
fact that the Standard Operating Procedure
(SOP) followed by Ordnance Factory
Board (OFB),was deficient before the
Board Meeting held on 28 February 2017;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
agenda discussed and deliberated in the
meeting as regards the signing of MoU with
Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM);
(c) whether Government has suddenly
found the SoP followed by OFB to be
deficient; and
(d) if so, why was so much time wasted
on this project and the Government's view
thereon?
Use of Army for civilian tasks
3367. SHRI AHAMED HASSAN: Will
the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has involved
the Army and para-military forces in
civilian tasks, if so, the details thereof; and
(b) whether Government is justified in
using Army engineers to build railway
bridges in Mumbai, if so, the reasons
therefor?
Exodus of scientists from DRDO
3368. SHRI HARSHVARDHAN
SINGH DUNGARPUR: Will the Minister
of DEFENCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Defence
Research and Development Organisation
(DRDO), which is engaged in developing
state-of-the-art weaponry for the armed
forces, has been facing an exodus of
scientists over a period of time;

790
(b) if so, the details thereof along with
the number of scientists who resigned from
DRDO between 2014 and 2017; and
(c) the steps taken/being taken by
Government to stop the exodus?

re-employment and self-employment for
